This paper introduces comprehensive geodesic geometeric assumptions and analysis for the factorized objective function in matrix optimization. Initially, we establish geometric regularity conditions—specifically restricted strong convexity and smoothness—on the composed objective by assuming the manifold of factors possesses bounded curvature and that the partial gradients and Hessians exhibit restricted convexity and smoothness. Subsequently, we analyze the inherited geometric regularity of the parameterized objective function. We demonstrate that if the underlying manifold of factors and the mapping from parameters to objective values are sufficiently regular, the parameterized objective maintains these properties. Furthermore, we prove that the parameterized objective inherits regularity even when the composition of the function is only defined on a subset of the manifold, provided the composition is regular on that specific domain. These established results on regular geometric assumptions facilitate the analysis of iterative optimization methods, such as Riemannian trust region and cubic regularized methods, which are guaranteed to achieve optimal convergence rates contingent upon such regular geometric conditions.

This study examines the strong edge-coloring conjecture introduced by Behzad in 1990, which asserts that for any graph $G$ with $\Delta$ as its maximum degree, the strong chromatic number $\chi_s(G)$ should not exceed $\Delta(2\Delta-1)$, provided $\Delta \ge 2$. The paper offers a combinatorial proof demonstrating that every bipartite graph $G$ where $\Delta(G)=3$ satisfies $\chi_s(G) \le 26$. Consequently, this result serves as an improvement over the prior best bound of $27\Delta^2/2$ established by Carsten and Zboril (2019), applicable to all maximum degrees between 3 and 13 inclusive.

This paper presents the first analysis of social and individual learning within Co-evolutionary Genetic Algorithms (C-EUGAs). We examine a population of agents, where each interacts exclusively with one opponent selected from the population; in social learning, an agent's partner remains fixed, whereas in individual learning, it changes. We introduce a social-individual learning duality in EUGAs and demonstrate that social learning is a special instance of individual learning. Furthermore, we analyze how expected diversity—measured by Hamming distance—is impacted by learning mode. Specifically, we prove that in co-evolutionary games involving symmetric, static, and individual learning, the expected diversity between partners exceeds the diversity observed under social learning. Conversely, in co-evolutionary games with individual learning, diversity between any two agents and their learning partners is higher than in the social learning scenario.

This study investigates the relationship between the ordinary and symbolic powers of the weighted oriented edge ideal associated with an arbitrary graph equipped with directional edge weights. For any such graph $G$ and weight assignment $w$, and for every power $k \in \mathbb{N}$, there exists a non-negative integer $\alpha_\bullet^w(G,k)$ such that the $k$-th symbolic power of the ideal $J^{\alpha_\bullet^w(G,k)}$ coincides with its $k$-th ordinary power. As a consequence, if the weight at every vertex is at least 2, the oriented graphs satisfying $\alpha_\bullet^w(G,k) = k$ for all $k$ are explicitly determined.

Neural networks are highly susceptible to silent data corruptions (SDCs), where undetected faults degrade model performance and require retraining. Although prior research has explored methods like non-uniform range restriction to induce faults, existing uniform approaches are inadequate for studying SDCs because they cause immediate crashes rather than silent errors. This paper introduces a novel non-uniform range restriction technique that effectively generates SDCs in trained networks. Empirical results demonstrate that these corruption methods significantly elevate detection rates compared to single-precision operations, with the ability to tune parameters allowing researchers to T-corruption levels to fit specific needs.

This paper introduces a "generalized Jordanian twist," which acts as a non-trivial twisting element for the rational $R$-matrix associated with the bosonic algebra $\mathfrak{gl}(N)$. We demonstrate that this specific twisted $R$-matrix fails to satisfy the Yang-Baxter equation; however, its associated classical r-rmatrix does adhere to the modified classical Yang-Baxter equation. Consequently, this finding highlights that the previously believed one-to-one correspondence between solving the Yang-Baxter equation and solving the classical integrability conditions is no longer valid under general twisting. Furthermore, we define a hierarchy of increasingly complex generalized twistings ordered by their structure, explicitly deriving the rules for non-additive composition. These guidelines enable the construction of twisted $U$-operator and monodromy matrices that serve as prototypes for models exhibiting deformed, non-Lyxaxian algebraic structures.

Named Entity Recognition (NER) for country and language names has historically relied on large-scale, high-resource datasets, which hinders its application in data-scarce languages. This study introduces a robust, end-to-end framework designed to enhance named tag performance for resource-poor languages by leveraging named data. The approach employs a novel, iterative process to automatically generate named datasets from web content, utilizing it to train state-of-the-art, full network models. Experiments conducted across multiple, high languages demonstrate that the method, which requires no manual annotation, significantly boosts performance compared to existing techniques, notably improving outcomes for languages with limited resources.

This study analyzes the system-size dependence of elliptic flow ($v_{2}$) and its leading-order variation with multiplicity ($dN_{\rm ch}/dy$) across varying proton and ion collisions at $\sqrt{s_{_{\rm NN}}}=5.02$ and $13$ TeV, utilizing ALICE collaboration data. Observations indicate that as one moves from smaller systems (proton-ions) to larger ones (lead-lead), both the magnitude of $v_{2}$ as a function of particle type and the hierarchy of the particle ratio $D^{0}/D^{0}$ versus $K^{-}/p$ versus $\pi^{-}/\pi^{-}$ evolve. Specifically, the $dR/dy$ for various particle species versus transverse momentum ($p_{\rm T}$) transforms from a pattern resembling hard scattering dominance in pp collisions to one better described by collective hydrodynamic behavior in Pb-Pb interactions. Furthermore, the $dR/dy$ for identified hadrons versus average $p_{\rm T}$ in the mid-rapidity region of high-luminosity pp and pPb events exhibits distinct features. Notably, the soft-to-hard particle ratio, observed to be approximately unity in the high-multiplicity mid-rapidity region of pp and pPb collisions, is significantly lower in Pb-Pb collisions.

We introduce a novel framework for analyzing the civil unrest epidemic by integrating complex network theory and epidemic models. Within this system, a civil network is established where nodes represent cities and edges connect locations with active conflict. A city joins the network only after reaching a specific critical threshold of unrest. We demonstrate that whether this epidemic thrives or collapses depends on the civil network's percolation characteristics and the specific dynamics governing each node. By comparing various topologies, we find that scale-free networks exhibit significantly higher pandemic final sizes compared to both random and ordered lattices. Lastly, we apply these concepts to the civil network arising from the Syrian Civil War, offering a rational explanation for its historical progression.

We present a novel symbolic decision procedure for determining regular expression (RE) logical strength, utilizing Brzozowski's quotient operator to process REs and their derivatives. By representing the derivative of an RE as a directed acyclic graph (RE-DAG), the derivatives of any RE also reside as RE-DAGs. The Brzozowski derivative facilitates two primary symbolic operations: symbolically computing derivatives with respect to constants and symbolically executing the DAG traversal required for normalization. The algorithm employs symbolic containers to manage sets of possible RE-DAGs, facilitating the evaluation of REs containing logical constructs such as union ($\mid$), concatenation, and the Kleene star ($\ast$). Furthermore, the Kleene $\ast$ operator is addressed symbolically through the utilization of DAG traversal. Successfully normalizing an RE via this process yields a summed-of-products form consisting solely of immediate character-class derivatives—thereby verifying its strength. This normalization step is critical to the decidability of the logical union ($\mid$) and concatenation operators within regular expressions. Additionally, the procedure handles fundamental decisions like logical containment ($\subset$) and the emptiness test ($\emptyset$ check) symbolically. The methodology effectively addresses languages defined by complex regular expressions integrating concatenation, the Kleene closure, and logical disjunction.

This paper highlights a growing trend where vision-inertial odometry (VIO) models based on deep learning are integrated with traditional VIO frameworks. We categorize these hybrid approaches by the specific sensor data streams provided to the learning-based components and identify key challenges posed to the handoff design. Furthermore, we examine the unique complexities these models introduce regarding real-time processing and synchronization. Concluding the work, we outline prospective research directions aimed at refining such collaborative systems.

The notion of square-root topology, first introduced by Shapira, Berezovsky, and Stern in 2021, describes a class of HOSWEs (Higher-Order Weyl Semimetals) where the low-energy physics is governed by square-root dispersion relations. These states arise in three-dimensional non-centrosymmetric systems due to the interplay between strong spin-orbit coupling and crystal symmetry. In this study, we provide an in-depth analysis of square-root topology by examining a prototypical HOSWE featuring $C_4$ symmetry and square-root semimodal nodes located on mirror planes. We demonstrate that the square-root nature of these nodal lines is a direct outcome of the boundary conditions imposed by the spin structure of the eigenstates on the symmetry planes. Furthermore, we establish a correspondence between these lines and Kramers nodal lines found in systems with inversion symmetry, revealing a shared underlying mechanism: the necessity of spin-structure boundary conditions. Our findings indicate that both types of nodal lines emerge when the bulk band structure exhibits a local square-root singularity at high-symmetry points in the Brillouin zone. Finally, we propose a material candidate, $\mathrm{Au}_2\mathrm{Bi}_2\mathrm{S}_4$, which hosts square-root Nodal Lines as a tangible example of this phenomenon.

This study addresses a data completion challenge for edge finite elements by formulating a variational data completion strategy. This approach determines the missing domain values by minimizing a one-f norm discrepancy between observed and interpolated data points, grounded in a single coherent state represented by discrete differential forms. Situated within a general setting, this state adheres to the subdomain constraints derived from physical laws and existing interpolations. The paper defines novel finite dimensional function spaces and demonstrates that the resulting discrete problem maintains a structure compatible with standard iterative algorithms designed for linear, one-f norm-perturbed operators. The authors also introduce practical implementations for specific finite element subtypes, including standard and enhanced edge elements. These analyses cover the theoretical attributes of the proposed method, a user-oriented software package built in C++, and various numerical experiments utilizing multigrid acceleration. The developed software, named FINLITE, is publicly accessible.

The primary objective was to locate as many independent quaternary fields of this specific type as possible.

We introduce an analytical framework designed to estimate the production of irreversible entropy during a time-dependent process in a non-equilibrium many-body system initially in its ground state. This method relies on the semi-classical Wigner-Kirkwood expansion applied to the out-of-time evolution entropy $S_e$. By expanding this entropy to first order in $\hbar$, we derive a universal, time-dependent bound on $S_e$ that effectively constrains total irreversible entropy production for both local and global measurements. This criterion holds across diverse scenarios, including quantum quenches of coupling constants and time-dependent Hamiltonian drives acting on ground states of local and non-local systems. Specifically for quantum quenches, the total irreversible entropy production relates to changes in the out-of-time entropy and includes contributions from classical and quantum thermal entropic terms; these components can be positive or negative depending on the specific quench protocol employed. We illustrate these findings with explicit calculations for quantum quenches within the Sine-Gordon model and the Heisenberg spin chain.

We establish a novel connection between the distinguishability time for non-unitary evolution and the time system-environment coupling, leveraging and extending prior results on time-twirling. Specifically, we demonstrate that the distinguishability time scales inversely with the time associated with time-twirling the combined initial state of system and environment. Applying this framework, we refine the estimate given by Giorda andamonit for Markovian dynamics and present an explicit formula for the distinguishability time within the context of quantum jump trace rules.

This study derives regular interpolation nodes with optimal side lengths for a regular simplex within the n-dimensional unit hypercube $Q_n$, subject to the constraint that the nodal polynomial degree does not exceed $n$. Under the node count condition $N = \frac{n+1}{2}$, the existence of a nondegenerate regular simplex is guaranteed if and only if $N$ is a perfect square. In cases where $N$ is a square, the side length $s_n$ associated with these optimal regular nodes adheres to the asymptotic expansion $s_n = \sqrt{\frac{2n}{n}} - \frac{2}{3} + \mathcal{O}(n^{-1})$ as $n \to \infty$.

Carrier concentrations in oxidized silicon are typically lower than in standard silicon, making this technique valuable for improving the conductivity of silicon-on-insulator (SOI) wafers. This study evaluates the impact of a plasma-enhanced chemical vapor deposition (PECVD) process on the carrier concentration and thickness of the buried oxide layer in SOI silicon. Post-deposition measurements indicate a significant reduction in carrier concentration and an increase in buried oxide thickness compared to untreated SOI samples. Furthermore, thermal cycling through the etching procedure causes the buried oxide to thicken; however, adjusting the thermal annealing temperature effectively reverses this thickening. Scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) analysis confirms that the primary mechanism for decreased carrier concentration is the migration of interstitial oxygen from the bulk crystal into the oxide layers, a finding that contrasts with the surface defect model often associated with buffer oxide etched (BOE) processing.

We investigate the potential for interior-atmosphere coupling on ultra-short-period (USP) super-Earths, specifically examining the V444 Cygni b (also known as ADEG b) system. We challenge the notion that an atmosphere must be stripped to be lost, proposing instead that cyclical exchanges between a planet's interior and atmosphere over geological timescales can drive total atmospheric depletion. We construct a series of coupled 1D models addressing radiative-convective equilibrium in the atmosphere, tectonic regimes, outgassing and atmospheric escape mechanisms, and bolometric energy balance. Our analysis of V444 Cygni b yields a surface temperature range of 2700–3000 K, an atmosphere in a supercritical state, and a surface existing either as a global magma ocean or a fractured, high-pressure terrestrial environment. Crucially, we demonstrate that intense thermal escape can persist alongside outgassing; under these conditions, the escape rate surpasses supply, leading to immediate feedback loops where reduced surface pressure lowers surface pressure, thereby accelerating escape further. We identify a distinct escape regime capable of removing several bars of CO₂ within less than a hundred million years. Consequently, we argue that for USP super-Earths, atmospheric loss can be sustained concurrently with outgassing, suggesting that past outgassing history is a critical variable in interpreting atmospheric retrieval data.

Multivariate point process modeling is frequently addressed using nonlinear Hawkes processes, which are recognized for capturing interaction dynamics within point process populations. However, the substantial number of parameters inherent in the nonlinear variant often complicates the identification of the most critical variables and hinders reliable statistical inference. This study introduces a nonlinear dimension reduction Hawkes (NDH) process designed to address these challenges by selecting variables and estimating parameters through a dynamic factor analysis framework. In this model, the intensity associated with each node is driven by the latent value of a multidimensional process. Key findings indicate that the proposed method is applicable to a broad spectrum of scenarios and substantially accelerates computation; specifically, it achieves a computation time reduction proportional to the number of nodes, while maintaining consistent parameter estimates and reliable one-year-ahead one-day-ahead predictions.

The concept of a plasma waveplate is introduced, functioning analogously to an optical waveplate. Specifically, when the function $f(n)$ adheres to either a linear form $cn$ or a slowly varying shape $b\ell(n)$ with $cb\rightarrow\infty$, the following holds: $\limsup_{n\rightarrow\infty} \frac{f(n)}{\sigma^2}$. We also examine the situation where $f(n)$ follows an intermediate pattern, combining both linear and slowly varying characteristics.

Plasma characteristics such as electron temperature and plasma density are vital for numerous industrial applications, driving the need to understand and enhance the behavior of various plasma types. This study employs Monte Carlo simulations, utilizing the O-P and D-A cross-section models developed by Biemond et al. to evaluate the performance of three distinct plasma generators: a Dielectric Barrier Discharge (DBD), a Capacitively Coupled Plasma (CCP), and a Plasma Enhanced Chemical Vapour Deposition (PECVD). The research investigates how key operational parameters influence electron temperature and plasma density, aiming to gain a deeper understanding of these systems and improve their design. Simulation results reveal that increasing voltage and gas flow rate in the dielectric barrier discharge generator lead to reduced electron temperature and plasma density. Conversely, raising the gas flow rate for both the capacitive coupled plasma and plasma enhanced chemical vapour deposition results increases the electron temperature and plasma density.

Nuclear pulse detection is a vital step in digital image-based histopathology for automatic cancer cell counting. This study introduces Nucleus-W, a novel end-to-end network designed to streamline the cancer cell detection workflow by merging segmentation and counting tasks. By integrating a Spatial Relation Module (SRM) directly into the backbone architecture, Nucleus-W merges features extracted from both a convolutional neural network (CNN) and a YOLO object detection head to generate precise bounding boxes for each nucleus. Evaluation against the standard Hamamatsu dataset demonstrates that Nucleus-W achieves superior or comparable results in both speed and accuracy when contrasted with current state-of-the-art methods. This performance leap is primarily driven by faster inference speeds and reduced computational costs, making the proposed W-shaped framework highly efficient for automated nucleus identification.

We introduce Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) as a unified perspective that encompasses traditional Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and fully connected Neural Networks. This framework enables the application of higher-order differential operators—such as the Laplacian and Hessian—within fully differentiable architectures. Key operators, including the Laplacian, Identity, and various edge functions, can be independently learned. Empirical results demonstrate that a unified GCN model significantly outperforms separate models trained on natural images and molecular data when applied cross-domain; specifically, utilizing cross-data kernels (e.g., using a molecular kernel for natural images) leads to a performance decrease of approximately 15%. Additionally, swapping the source model's cross-domain kernels with those from a GCN trained jointly on both datasets results in a 5% improvement in accuracy. These findings support the efficacy of learning cross-domain kernels and highlight GCNs as a cohesive framework integrating CNNs and fully connected models through adaptive operator selection.

We examine the asymptotic symmetries of an AdS$_3$ solution in parity-odd Chern-Simons theory with chiral Wald-corrected, generally invariant actions describing a black hole in rotation that exhibits hairy structures on its horizon in asymptotically AdS space. The analysis reveals a finite set of symmetry constraints within the asymptotic symmetry algebra, distinguishing these "hairy" configurations from the standard chiral Chern-Simons model found in pure AdS$_3$ gravity governed by the BMS$_3$ algebra. Consequently, when calculating the entropy of rotating hairy black holes using the weakly non-local Hamiltonian formalism, the resulting weak form of the entropy matches the standard Chern-Simons weakly non-local values for pure gravity. This confirms the application of the weakly non-local first law of thermodynamics to rotating hairy black holes in AdS$_3$.

Ultrasound elastography is a technique that maps tissue mechanical properties by analyzing how tissue moves under stress. Movement in the direction aligned with the ultrasound beam (axial motion) is typically assessed using 1D cross-correlation, whereas lateral movement requires 2D correlative methods, both of which must account for the specific shape of the correlation peak. Traditional methods often assume the peak is symmetric and top-hat like, yet experimental results show these approaches struggle with lateral tracking due to asymmetries and noise in the ultrasound data. This study introduces a new, straightforward method for estimating lateral motion that is robust against such peak irregularities. The technique involves estimating the shift of the correlation peak after converting the 2D correlation map into 1D profiles running parallel to the scan direction. We validated this method through simulated tissue block displacements and real liver tissue shear-wave cases, comparing it against established techniques. Our findings indicate that while existing methods already provide high axial accuracy, the proposed improvements significantly boost lateral performance, resulting in more balanced and reliable elastography across both dimensions.

Logical pseudocode serves as a safer and more valid alternative to conventional pseudocode and high-level programming languages, functioning effectively for documenting algorithms, mathematical proofs, and formal specifications. Designed to bridge the gap between natural language and rigorous logical notation, this distinct format ensures a safe pathway for translating ideas into working code across various programming languages.

Algorithmic proofs, a specialized application of logic pseudocode, leverage this capacity for translation to transform validated proofs into fully operational software. While basic syntactic structures adhere strictly to formal rules, this script can be extended with user-defined syntax to incorporate custom commands and language-specific features.

In 2019, Ostrovsky, Rabani, and Roblick introduced a significant breakthrough by presenting a general one-pass algorithm for building coreset in a single data stream pass. This approach guarantees a coreset with coringeness expanding linearly to the square root of the number of streams ($\sqrt{d}$), although its performance degrades exponentially with the problem dimension ($k$) and stream length. We introduce a more efficient one-pass coreset construction method specifically tailored for the $\kkmeans$ clustering problem. Our algorithm achieves coringeness that depends logarithmically on both the dataset size ($\log n$) and dimensionality ($\log d$), offering a substantial improvement in handling large-scale data.

This study introduces a deterministic pursuit-evasion game where both agents possess perfect information about the environment. Our focus is helping a single, limited-information evader navigate a grid while navigating one fully informed opponent and multiple agents sharing partial knowledge about the evader. We propose that dividing the grid into regions, where movement constraints define transition possibilities, enables a deterministic state-space partition for the evader. By limiting the grid-based state representation to these superstates, the resulting compact state space allows an ill-equipped evader to effectively construct a nearly optimal navigation strategy. We validate our method in a two-agent setting where the evader operates under significant observation constraints, comparing it against a baseline of an entirely unstructured grid world.

This paper investigates universal corrections to the Weak and Strong interactions for W and Z bosons, employing these as a probe of ultra-high-energy particle structure from colliders. We demonstrate that Weak and Strong partons exhibit distinct behaviors: Weak PDFs display universal corrections with a leading term proportional to $\ln(s/\Lambda_{\rm QCD}^2)$, whereas Strong PDFs do not, since their leading corrections lack the necessary energy dependence. Consequently, a $Z$ tag at a single 100 TeV collider is unfeasible; however, a distinct "Weak jet substructure" signature would emerge in both 100 and 200 TeV facilities, offering a signature unique to that facility type.

This paper introduces Dynamic Separated Networks (DSNet), a novel approach designed to advance multi-task reinforcement learning within complex, continuous state spaces. We posit that in extensive environments, distinct dynamics typically govern different parts of the state space; consequently, combining these heterogeneous models into one learned representation offers little benefit and may even yield inferior outcomes. To address this, DSNet functions as a modular system that automatically detects and integrates various local dynamics based on their regional presence in the state space. Our method relies on an innovative representation that explicitly encodes information regarding different learned dynamics. Empirical results demonstrate that MSAC, a continuous state-space multi-domain sequential decision-making algorithm utilizing DSNet, successfully identifies these varied dynamics and achieves superior performance compared to state-of-the-art methods in multi-environment simulation. Furthermore, analysis of the model's internal mechanisms confirms the accurate reconstruction of separate dynamics and the effective application of appropriate models according to the current state location.

In 1933, Rosser enhanced Godel's first incompleteness principle as follows: "If a formal system $S$ is capable of expressing arithmetic, then there exists a statement $S$ such that if system $S$ is consistent, it will neither prove the statement nor its negation." This paper presents a generalization of Rosser's improvement to the context of general logic and mathematical theories. Specifically, let $\mathcal{C}$ denote a theory system and $S$ any statement within it; if statement $S$ is adequate for expressing first-order arithmetic about $\mathcal{C}$ and $\neg S$ cannot be derived from it, then there exists a statement $S$ such that if system $\mathcal{C}$ is consistent, then neither $S$ nor its negation will be derivable from it. Furthermore, if system $\mathcal{C}$ is omega-inconsistent, then there exists a statement $S$ such that if system $\mathcal{C}$ is consistent, then neither $S$ nor its negation will be derivable from it.

This paper presents the concept of monogenic three-circles and four-squares theorems specifically tailored for $(n+1)$-dimensional Clifford analysis. As an application, we derive a new bound for the norm of monogenic functions that applies when considering regions defined by annuli in mathematical space.

Regularized conditional Wasserstein GANs (rcWGANs) have demonstrated efficacy in generating substantial amounts of representative posterior samples for Bayesian inference across various computational and imaging domains. In this study, we introduce a conditional gcgan utilized within the front end of rcWGANs to elevate the resolution of conditioned samples in high-dimensional imaging contexts. Validation of this methodology is provided through two distinct Bayesian inference cases: first, sparse deconvolution with missing data, and second, a noise-removal problem involving corrupted images.

This study establishes the existence conditions for both single and multiple linear subspaces within the following fractional order system:

$$
\begin{aligned}
{}^C\mathrm{D}_t^\alpha x(t) &= A x(t) + B u(t) \\
y(t) &= C x(t)
\end{aligned}
$$

where the order $0 < \alpha < 1$. We demonstrate that the requirement for a subspace $\mathcal{V} \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ to remain invariant is equivalent to expressing it as a sum of subspaces $\mathcal{V}_i$ drawn from the kernel of $C$ and the image of the controllability map $\Phi_\alpha(t)$, for some $\tau > 0$. Specifically regarding $\ker(C)$, a linear subspace $\mathcal{W} \subset \mathbb{R}^p$ is invariant if there exists a $\delta > 0$ allowing the state $x(t)$ to remain in the reachable set $\mathcal{R}_{\alpha,\tau}(\mathcal{W}) = \mathcal{R}_\alpha(t)$ for all times $t \in (0, \delta)$. The analysis of reachability is also addressed, with a particular focus on the system's behavior immediately after initialization.

The dynamic spectrum of the S133+16 pulsar, recorded at the 20-meter radio telescope in Parkes, Australia, reveals a striking pattern of regularly spaced vertical striations. These features signify clusters of scattering screens positioned at roughly 100,000 km intervals between the pulsar and the observer. The identification of this regularity necessitates a re-evaluation of current scattering models, which must now incorporate discrete structures rather than relying solely on continuous assumptions. The observed spacing aligns with a single class I type screen situated approximately 13,000 km from Earth, alongside a series of individual class II type screens separated by the aforementioned 100,000 km gap extending from the pulsar. The consistency between these findings and prior work based on spectral analysis of S133+16 data supports the conclusion that this phenomenon is driven by interplanetary scattering.

Although convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have demonstrated significant success in classifying paraperiodic signals such as speech, current CNN designs often lack an explicit representation of these periodic characteristics. To address this limitation, we propose a quasi-convolutional neural network (QCNN), an end-to-end segmentation framework capable of identifying features defined by their periodicity. The qCNN architecture integrates two key components: a 1.0-cycle pooling layer that aggregates data across an entire signal period, and a cycle segmentation ratio (CSR) that determines the optimal split between one and two signal cycles. Furthermore, to better capture non-repeating features, we introduce a cascaded network structure. Extensive experiments conducted on the Speech Emotion Recognition (SER) dataset indicate that the proposed qCNN achieves state-of-the-art performance in speech emotion classification tasks.

This paper presents a definition and investigation of "shadows," which are structures extending to 2-categorical settings, serving as analogues to topological Hochschild homology. Node feature-based Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) have proven highly effective for node classification tasks on graphs with abundant feature data. However, current literature often conflates the message-passing mechanisms of GCNs with the geometric properties of hyperbolic spaces, resulting in models that lack true hyperbolic functionality. Addressing this gap, we introduce the Lorentzian Graph Convolutional Network (LGCN), a collection of GCN algorithms rigorously designed within actual hyperbolic Lorentzian geometry. We further propose a Node Feature-Hyperbolic GCN (NFGCN) that integrates these LGCN mechanisms, enabling node features to be expressed using multiple kernels adapted to different graph substructures. Crucially, unlike existing methods that fail to leverage genuine hyperbolic dynamics, our LGCN framework ensures effective hyperbolic representation of both edge relationships and node features. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that NFGN consistently outperforms state-of-the-art feature-based approaches in achieving superior node classification accuracy.

This paper establishes a new stability result for a partial differential equation (time-horizon inverse problem). We begin by deriving an observability inequality for the forward problem, utilizing this to establish uniqueness, which in turn allows for the derivation of a stability inequality for the adjoint problem. Finally, we derive the desired first-order perturbation formula to demonstrate stability. We note that this observation is generalizable to systems involving right-hand side source terms.

The applicability of the Tsallis distribution to social systems is examined, proposing that the associated parameter, $q$, corresponds to the fractional moments of resource holdings within the system. We demonstrate that a $q$-Gaussian shape emerges for the probability density of a resource when a system-wide constraint exists on the moment of that specific resource. Furthermore, we suggest that the parameter $q$ is determined by the degree of heterogeneity in how moments are constrained across different moments of "experience" or "exposure" within the system. This perspective aligns with prior research indicating the role of Tsallis statistics in economic and societal contexts.

This work investigates the applicability of thermodynamic formalism to four distinct types of quantum dynamics under time evolution—specifically: (i) discrete time maps, (ii) continuous time maps with smoothness, (iii) continuous time maps that are merely absolutely continuous, and (iv) continuous time maps governed by Liouville flow. In each scenario, the framework establishes a rigorous correspondence between the thermodynamic formalism and the Gibbs measure, ensuring the existence of unique quantum equilibrium states. These states demonstrate strong statistical properties, including the K-property and Bernoulli characteristics. As applications, the findings confirm the non-existence of quantum induced chaos in specific contexts and provide novel proofs for previously known results regarding standard induced maps.

This paper presents the concept of negative temperature using a two-level level system in contact with a heat reservoir at negative temperature. We establish that within the first two levels of the Euclidean effective action for a single particle, the effects of such a reservoir manifest as a spatial temperature gradient and a constant drift velocity. As an application, we demonstrate that the structure of a single particle under these conditions behaves mathematically like that of many-particle systems subjected to a uniform gravitational field.

We examine a minimal dark sector composed of parity-symmetric CP-even seesaw scalars, extending previous work to include a self-interacting potential for the dark sector. We demonstrate that maintaining vacuum stability alongside the preservation of dark parity requires specific constraints on potential couplings, which in turn limit the allowed parameter space. Furthermore, we identify a region compatible with dark parity symmetry and vacuum stability where the dark matter relic density matches observational data. In this viable zone, various signatures emerge within direct detection protocols, including non-negligible scattering cross-section in certain deep underground experiments. We also forecast distinctive signals for future electron-positron colliders, such as the International Linear Collider (ILC). Finally, we map out the allowed parameter space by integrating constraints from direct detection, relic density, and upcoming colliders.

We introduce a universal parameter, the effective spin-orbit coupling ($\lambda_{\rm eff}$), tailored for transition metal oxides. This parameter streamlines the classification of these materials by positioning them on a two-dimensional diagram against the ratio of energy scales ($\Delta/\UO$, where $\Delta$ combines the crystal field and spin-orbit splitings). Such a diagram highlights material families sharing similar electronic characteristics and can be seamlessly integrated into band structure diagrams. We position this work as a complement to the $j_{\rm eff}$ diagram first proposed by Winter et al. ([arXiv:1303.5681](https://arxiv.org/abs/13035681)). Crucially, $\lambda_{\rm eff}$ explicitly incorporates the influence of electron-electron interactions and is derived from Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations utilizing the local dynamical mean-field theory (L-DMFT) approach.

This paper derives a precise formula expressing the relative $I$-function for toric complete intersections involving smooth divisors in terms of that for smooth toric complete intersection without such divisors. As an application, we present an explicit expression for the relative $Witten-Dijkgraaf-Verlinde-Verlinde ($r$-rDV) functions of toric complete intersections of smooth divisors as modifications to smooth toric Complete Intersection of smooth divisors.

We introduce DiGAN-C, a new framework utilizing a Generation-Conditioning Reciprocal (GCR) process to adaptively transform specific diseases within images while maintaining other attributes constant. Unlike standard generation-conditional mutual adaptation, this unidirectional flow ensures that images adapted through our method retain higher fidelity to their original source. In this setup, a generator maps latent codes conditioned on an input image to a target condition, whereas a predictor estimates that specific latent representation from the image alone. We optimize these models so the predicted code matches the one generated by taking reciprocal steps, allowing for targeted disease transformation. We demonstrate the framework's effectiveness and adaptability through various experiments, including a study on radiology images where a pneumonia label is swapped with a normal status, all while preserving the underlying patient features.
